title: Aphrody OS: Bun runtime and native SDK architecture
summary: The Bun fork, shared native C ABI and TypeScript SDK behind Aphrody OS, with separate source and deployment contracts.
content:
# Aphrody OS runtime and native SDK

Aphrody OS brings a browser interface, a desktop shell and a cross-platform CLI around shared capability owners. The runtime comes from the private `aphrody-labs/bun` fork. Product workflows and the canonical interface remain in the Aphrody monorepo.

## Bun runtime

Bun provides the JavaScriptCore runtime, Web APIs, bundler, package manager and test runner. Fork API documentation lives in the fork's `docs/` tree. Aphrody records its selected documentation revision in `docs/reference/upstream-bun/SOURCE.json`; it does not maintain a second Bun documentation tree.

## Native SDK

`packages/engine/runtime` declares `@aphrody/runtime-sdk`. Its FFI loader uses `dlopen` from `bun:ffi`. The native library boundary is `aphrody_ffi` in `crates/interop/ffi`, and `include/aphrody.h` retains the `aphrody_*` and `yolo_*` compatibility identities. The ABI contract requires version checks, opaque handles and library-owned buffer release.

## Qualification

Source declarations do not prove that every native module is installed or active on every platform. Check the selected artifact, ABI and target before enabling a native capability.

## Source references

- [Aphrody architecture and active plan](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/PLAN.md)
- [Native ABI header](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/crates/interop/ffi/include/aphrody.h)
- [Runtime SDK](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/tree/main/packages/engine/runtime)
- [Bun fork documentation](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/bun/tree/main/docs)

title: Bun, Next.js and Tailwind in the Aphrody UI
summary: Where runtime tooling and UI adapters are owned, and how the canonical web and desktop interface is built.
content:
# Bun and the Aphrody UI

The Bun fork owns runtime changes, built-in modules and Bun build tooling. Aphrody owns application behavior and the canonical UI in `m3/packages/app-ui`.

## Shared interface

The app-ui package contains product documentation, project templates and application routes. Its build script produces the frontend consumed by the native site and desktop shell. The former `apps/web` checkout is retired and is not the current build entry point.

## Framework adapters

`m3/packages/m3-next` contains the Next.js adapter. Tailwind and Material 3 packages have their own manifests and build contracts. Consult the selected package and Bun fork documentation before choosing an API; package presence does not prove production activation or comparative performance.

## Source references

title: Material 3 color tokens and dynamic themes
summary: Seed-based color schemes and semantic tokens in Aphrody's Material 3 packages, with contrast checks for the rendered interface.
content:
# Material 3 color tokens

Aphrody's Material 3 framework separates semantic color roles from component styling. `m3/packages/m3-tokens/src/dynamic-color.ts` exposes seed-based scheme utilities including `schemeFromSeed`, `cssFromSeed` and `applyDynamicColor`.

## HCT and semantic roles

HCT represents hue, chroma and tone. A seed and scheme configuration resolve roles such as primary, surface and their associated foreground colors. Components consume roles rather than assuming that one hexadecimal value fits every theme.

## Contrast and accessibility

Theme configuration is not a blanket accessibility guarantee. Check contrast, keyboard navigation, focus indicators and readable text in the rendered light and dark interfaces, including custom component states.

## Source references

- [Dynamic color implementation](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/m3/packages/m3-tokens/src/dynamic-color.ts)
- [Material color system](https://m3.material.io/styles/color/overview)
- [Google web accessibility guidance](https://web.dev/learn/accessibility/)

title: Aphrody desktop: CEF, Tauri and the shared UI bridge
summary: The canonical desktop shell, its frontend configuration and the RPC shared with the web application.
content:
# Aphrody desktop and the shared UI

The desktop shell lives in `crates/ui/app`. Its manifest selects `tauri-runtime-cef`; its Tauri configuration sets `frontendDist` to `ui-dist` and declares the main window. The canonical frontend lives in `m3/packages/app-ui`.

## Shared RPC

`m3/packages/app-ui/src/tauri-bridge.ts` routes `aphrodyRpc` through the `aphrody_rpc` desktop command inside Tauri and through same-origin `POST /rpc` in the browser. The app-server requires an initialization handshake. Studio also contains explicitly registered native commands; a web route does not automatically gain desktop privileges.

## Deployment boundary

A configured frontend and a compiled shell are separate from an installed application running on a physical desktop. Check the installed artifact and its supported target before claiming native activation. The former `apps/web` ping bridge is not the current architecture.

## Source references

- [Desktop shell](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/tree/main/crates/ui/app)
- [Desktop configuration](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/crates/ui/app/tauri.conf.json)

title: Aphrody agent context, llms.txt and isolated memory
summary: Repository guidance, public AI-readable context and domain-isolated memory, without implicit provider synchronization.
content:
# Agent context and isolated memory

`AGENTS.md` defines repository conventions and capability ownership. `PLAN.md` records the active architecture and queue, while `MEMORY.md` records dated evidence and limits. These files guide coding agents; they do not change model training.

## Public context

The live `https://aphrody.com/llms.txt` endpoint returned an Aphrody overview during the 2026-10-09 audit. Treat it as a public context document rather than a guarantee of search indexing, ranking or deployment completeness.

## Native memory

`aphrody home` and `aphrody graph` provide the native home and graph surfaces. The `aphrody`, `dbfr` and `ie` profiles remain isolated. Provider authentication, cookies and raw provider histories stay in their protected stores; no provider-memory synchronization is implied.

## Source references

- [Public llms.txt](https://aphrody.com/llms.txt)
- [Repository guidance](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/AGENTS.md)
- [Active architecture](https://github.com/aphrody-labs/aphrody/blob/main/PLAN.md)
